name: spatial_vs_wellmixed_community
title: Spatial structure vs well-mixed community
claim: A well-mixed microbial community drives glucose to complete exhaustion, whereas a spatially-structured community scenario plateaus with a large standing glucose pool unconsumed at the same horizon — an observed difference in substrate-use completeness between well-mixed and spatial community scenarios.

purpose.question: Does spatial structure change how completely a microbial community consumes its shared substrate, compared with the well-mixed case?
purpose.mechanism: New biology-forward study (discovery engine): a new configuration/analysis of a real spatio-flux composite.
purpose.expected_outcome: The quantitative behavior tests pass, confirming the stated emergent/metabolic claim.

question: Does spatial structure change how completely a microbial community consumes its shared substrate, compared with the well-mixed case?

behavior_tests.name: SPATIAL-VS-WELLMIXED-WELLMIXED-DEPLETES
behavior_tests.description: the well-mixed community drives glucose to near-zero.

behavior_tests.name: SPATIAL-VS-WELLMIXED-SPATIAL-RETAINS-POOL
behavior_tests.description: the spatial community scenario retains a substantial standing glucose pool (does not reach complete depletion) at the run horizon.

findings.statement: Run to the same horizon, the well-mixed community consumes essentially all of its glucose (10 -> ~0) while the spatial community scenario plateaus with a large standing pool unconsumed (300 -> ~83, ~72% consumed): the spatial arrangement reaches a less complete substrate use. The two arms are DIFFERENT composites with different initial glucose, so this is a scenario-level observation, not a controlled isolation of spatial structure (see limitations).

resolved: Spatial structure leaves substrate unconsumed that a well-mixed community would fully deplete.
remaining: Whether stronger mixing (higher diffusion) recovers the well-mixed depletion is unquantified.

followup_study_proposals.motivation: If spatial structure leaves substrate unused, does increasing diffusion (mixing) interpolate back to the well-mixed full-depletion limit?

falsifiability: If the spatial arrangement depleted glucose as completely as the well-mixed community (final glucose ~0), the 'spatial structure changes substrate use' claim would be false.
limitations: The well-mixed (community_dfba) and spatial (spatial_dfba_process) arms are DIFFERENT composites with different species sets, biomass representations, and ~30x different initial glucose (10 vs 300). The contrast is therefore scenario-level, not a controlled spatial-vs-well-mixed isolation.
Completeness is read from final glucose at one horizon; no fraction-matched or mixing-swept control.

alternative_hypotheses.hypothesis: The incomplete consumption in the spatial arm is due to its different composite / larger initial glucose, not spatial structure per se.
alternative_hypotheses.excluded_by: NOT excluded — this is an acknowledged confound (see limitations). The claim is intentionally limited to the observed scenario-level difference; a matched-initial, same-composite spatial-vs-mixed control is proposed as the follow-up.

alternative_hypotheses.hypothesis: The spatial run simply needs more time to finish depleting glucose.
alternative_hypotheses.excluded_by: Both conditions run to the same horizon and the spatial glucose is gradient-limited (far-from-source sites never access it).
